_comment: Lint ratchet baseline. Checked by scripts/lint-ratchet.mjs from the CI
`lint` job: the count may fall, never rise. See CI-LINT-PLAN.md.
`fatals` is tracked separately, and ratcheted separately, because a fatal
is a PARSE failure rather than a rule finding — the file was not linted at
all, so it contributes zero errors and looks clean by the only number the
ratchet would otherwise read. Both workspaces are at 0 and must stay there.
The backend sat at 120 fatals until Phase 4: tsconfig.json excludes
src/**/__tests__/** and src/**/*.test.ts, and a file outside
parserOptions.project is a fatal, not a skip, so every test file failed to
parse. backend/.eslintrc.json now points at tsconfig.eslint.json, which
extends the production config and drops only those two excludes. The
production tsconfig.json is untouched, so nothing changed about what is
emitted to dist/. Admitting 120 files is what took backend errors/warnings
from 5658/277 to 6293/408 — a deliberate re-baseline, not a regression.
Phase 5 then began bringing it down for real: the first pass typed three
DB/Mongo boundary files and took errors 6293 -> 6062. The numbers recorded
below are the live ones; this prose is not, so trust the fields.
A fatal reappearing means some file is outside parserOptions.project again.
Fix the project reference; do not re-baseline around it.
To lower the counts after real cleanup:
cd backend && npm run -s lint:json | node ../scripts/lint-ratchet.mjs backend --update
